title: A puzzle game's description, or a library of techniques
description: What `src/describe/load.ts` validates every `*.description.yaml` against. Every string marked a formula is in the formula syntax of docs/descriptions.md § "The formula syntax", and the compiler parses each. Every string marked prose is markdown.

rung.description: The game's hint rungs a firing of this is recorded under, among its hintRungs: one, or several where one firing records under more than one (an Unequal sign's two ends).

from.description: A tier above the technique's own, on its scale: the ladder runs it only at a cap that high, and a firing grades at its own tier. Solo's reading of the partial cages the region rule works out grades as a cage's reading, and only where the region rule is in reach.

until.description: A tier above the technique's own: at a cap that high the ladder does not run it, where a technique there strikes all it does and a grade should not rest on the weaker one.

statement.description: What a technique says, wherever it is stated.

on.description: The engine runs it as each value is placed (`place`), or as a fact strikes a value from a cell (`strike`), with its first binder bound to that cell, and not as a rung of the ladder. One run on striking only strikes.

for.description: The binders, as after `forall`: `x in S where P, y = t, ...`.

premise.description: Over the marks; absent is true.

conclude.description: `strike(c, d)` and `place(c, d)` facts, joined by `and`, under `forall` where it ranges.

says.description: What a hint step for a firing of this speaks of, each a formula over the technique's binding, read on the marks before the firing's facts are made (under the technique's own `with`).

shown.description: `each`: a step for every square the firing decides, each its own argument (its evidence is the outline less that square alone). Absent, one step for the firing.

terms.description: Named values the step's sentence reads, by name.

marks.description: The elements a step marks, by the role they are marked in: a set of cells. The firing's own facts are ringed without being said; evidence is the outline's set less them.

arms.description: Where a step reads differently by what holds of the binding: each arm is a name and a condition, tried in order, the first true one winning, and adds its own `terms` and `marks` to the shared ones above. The step's kind is `<id>.<arm>`.

tier.description: One of `tiers`, or of one of `scales`.

oneOf.description: A library's technique placed at a tier of this game's.

library.description: Techniques stated once, for every game that places them with `use`.

slots.description: One slot beyond each end of every row and column, seeing along it: `slots`, `sight(s)`, `opposite(s)`.

edges.description: The orthogonal pairs: `edges`, `ends(e)`, `end1(e)`, `end2(e)`, `other(e, c)`, `edge(a, b)`. `king` adds the diagonal pairs, and `crossedBy(e)`, the other diagonal of the four squares a diagonal edge crosses (none for an orthogonal one).

corners.description: Every point inside the grid where four cells meet: `corners`, `cells(k)`, `corners(c)`, `across(k, c)`.

points.description: Every point where cells meet, the border's included: `points`, `cells(k)`, `points(c)`, `slash(c, k)` (the value, 1 or 2, of `c`'s diagonal through `k`), `linked(k)` (the points the cells' diagonals join to `k`).

centers.description: Every center inside the grid a square can be turned about, a square's middle, a side's or a point where four meet: `centers`, `cells(p)` (the squares round it), `opp(c, p)` (the square `c` turns to about `p`, half a turn, or none off the grid).

diagonals.description: The two diagonals of a square grid: `diagonals`.

regions.description: Named partitions of the cells: `dealt`, from the board, or a library partition such as `blocks(rw, rh)`.

relations.description: A planning game's relations the board deals, each a set of cells for each cell, read `name(c)`.

tiling.description: A board that is a tiling the deal decides (Loopy's), in place of `grid`: its cells are the dots, `edges` join them (`edges(c)` a dot's, in its turn), and two sorts of element more, `faces` (`cells(f)` and `edges(f)` round a face, `faces(e)` either side of an edge) and `angles`, two edges side by side round a dot (`angles(c)` a dot's in its turn, `angles(f)` a face's, `edges(a)`, `apex(a)` its dot). Rows, columns, neighbors by direction and coordinates are refused on it. `square` where the tiling is always the grid of squares, the dots its squares (Pearl's): the techniques are checked on square tilings alone.

cells.description: A planning game's board that is not a rectangle: this many cells and no geometry, so `x`, `y`, `cell`, the neighbors, rays and lines are refused on it. In place of `grid`.

faces.description: A planning game's second sort of element: a size the board deals, how many faces. `faces` names them, and a layer `over: faces` holds a value a face.

tables.description: A planning game's tables the board deals, each a function of elements and numbers to an element, `none` where it has no value: read `name(a, ...)`, or `name` where it takes nothing.

units.description: The named sets of lines and regions in which no value repeats: `units`, `units_of(c)` and `peers(c)` read them.

define.description: Named terms and predicates, `name(params)` to a formula.

clues.description: Clue kinds: where one sits, its values, and what it means, reading `at` and `v`.

at.description: The element sort a clue sits at, or `board` for a whole-board clue, which has `fields` in place of a `value`.

per.description: A clue at the element for each value of the answer's domain, read `clue(kind, x, d)`; its meaning reads the value as `per`.

list.description: The clue at an element is a list of numbers, each one of `value`, in order: a line's run lengths. `clue(kind, x)` is the list, and its meaning reads it as `v`.

fields.description: A whole-board clue's parts, each read as a function of the clue, and of an element where it has an `at`: one a cell is `peg(k, s)`.

list.description: The field of a clue is a list of numbers, each one of `value`, in order: a number's digits. Read whole as `f(k)`, its length `|f(k)|`, and a member `nth(f(k), i)`, counted from 0.

complete.description: Every place carries one, so an absent clue is a fact.

domain.description: The values the layer may hold, read by the dead-end checker; `integers` for a domain that is not finite, which holds any integer a double holds exactly and is computed exactly.

checked.description: Of a layer whose domain is `integers`, the values the dead-end checker searches it over: a line of moves that leaves them ends there.

arranged.description: The layer is an arrangement: each value of its domain on this many cells. Read by the dead-end checker.

once.description: Exactly one cell holds this value, and every other another of the domain: a token, such as a ball. Read by the dead-end checker.

on.description: Where this formula of the cell `c`, which reads only layers at `c`, is false, the layer holds 0: a value stands only there. Read by the dead-end checker.

carried.description: A value a move copies and no rule reads, such as a barrel's letter: the compiler refuses a read of it but in an assignment to itself, and the dead-end checker holds it at 0.

over.description: The layer holds a value a face of `space.faces`, or one value for the whole board, read by its name alone, in place of a value a cell.

assignments.description: What a move sets: each entry's binders, the last of them the cell assigned, and a term for each layer it assigns, read on the position before the move. An entry with no binders assigns layers over the board.

deadEnds.description: Claims by id, each a formula over the position true only where no line of moves finishes: `Game.hasNoSolution`. Each is checked sound on small boards.

help.description: The game's help page, which `src/describe/help-page.ts` renders in this order: the title is the catalog's name, and every `#` and `##` heading and `{{parameters}}` are the renderer's.

sections.description: The game's own sections, each under its heading.

origins.description: Who invented the puzzle, its other names, where more of it is: under `## Where the puzzle comes from`, or `puzzles come` for a game with rulesets.

hints.description: Under `## Hints`: what the hint's marks mean here, and its words for them. Present exactly when the game has a hint.

parameters.description: Under `## <Name> parameters`, either side of the list generated from `paramConfig`.

game.description: A game's description: its help page, its formal rules, or both. The formal rules come whole.

then.description: A game's rules state an answer, or a planning game's position and its moves.

game.description: The id, as the app's registry has it, or a family's other game.

family.description: What the player produces (theory.md): latin, shading, loop, ...

sizes.description: The numbers that scale an instance, each a range.

sort.description: What holds a value: a cell, or the edge between two cells side by side (Separate's walls), where the space has its edges.

wide.description: Whether a value may run past 31, the most a mask of 32 bits holds: Ascent's number on a square, up to the board's square count. A cell's candidates are then read by membership, a count, the least and a binder, never as a set, and the domain is `range(a, b)` or `{d in range(a, b) where P}`.

to.description: The cell a cell's value names, a term of the cell `c` and the value `d`, none where it names none: what `to(c)` reads and `chain(c)` follows. Rome's arrows are `step(c, d)`; Signpost's links `compass(c, clue(arrow, c), d)`.

repeat.description: The one value of the domain that appears more than once in a unit, and how many times: `times(d)` reads it, 1 for every other value. Salad's empty square.

given.description: The answer functions the board may give values of: givens, not clues.

marks.description: What the player can write down.

of.description: For a mark on the edges, on a tiling's angles, or on the cells of an answer that is not on the cells, a technique reads: the number of the answer it narrows, read of the element `at`. The mark is read `name(e)`, the values it may still hold, and narrowed by `strike(e, d)`.

means.description: For a mark on the cells that names one clue (`notation: "one of clues(kind)"`): what the cell `at` naming the clue `v` says of the answer. The mark is read `name(c)`, the clue or none, and made by `mark(c, q)`.

views.description: A planning game's definitions the game reads beside its rules, each of cells, its last parameter the cell: the compiled module's `views` gives the cells each holds of, for values of the others.

kind.description: For a planning game, `permute` claims every move is legal everywhere and moves the pieces the same way on every position, which the dead-end checker checks; `transition` claims nothing.

position.description: A planning game's position: its layers, each a value a cell, by name, read in a formula as a function of a cell.

moves.description: A planning game's moves, by name, in the order a position's moves are listed.

for.description: Its arguments, as a technique's binders: plain numbers and elements.

when.description: Its guard, over the position; absent is true.

finish.description: Formulas over the position, all true of a finished one.

lose.description: Formulas over the position, any true of a lost one.

deal.description: What the generator chooses, in words: consumed by nothing yet.

tiers.description: The ladder, lowest first; the last is the search where the game has one.

scales.description: Grading scales besides `tiers`, each graded and capped on its own, by name: each its tiers, lowest first. A technique on one names one of its tiers.

variations.description: Blocks added to the description, or replacing its blocks of the same name, under the name the game offers it by: a modifier's words, or a ruleset's name. A variation that only adds is a modifier, and one that replaces is a ruleset. The compiler reads the description with every variation applied, so a technique may read what one deals, and finds it empty on a board without it.

space.description: Partitions of new names, units after the description's, and the diagonals.

position.description: A planning game's layers of new names, each all zeros on a board without the variation.

finish.description: A planning game's finish formulas, true of a finished position where the variation is on.

moves.description: Assignments added to a planning game's moves, by the move's name, made where the variation is on.

clues.description: Clue kinds of the same names, each replaced whole: Rect's Patches widens its number to a question mark.

position.description: A planning game's layers of the same names, replaced.
